items.snippet:
### Why is my funding valuation higher than what acquirers offer?

Because the t...
items.raw_snippet:
### Why is my funding valuation higher than what acquirers offer?

Because the two are priced on different logic. A round buys a minority stake and a claim on a wide range of future outcomes, with preferences and rights attached to protect the investor. An acquisition buys the whole company in cash, with the buyer taking execution risk. The gap is structural rather than evidence that acquirers are undervaluing you, and our note on what multiple a SaaS business sells for explains the mechanics. [...] ### The Questions That Actually Decide It

Strip out the valuation comparison and a handful of questions do most of the work. None has a general answer.

Would more capital change the outcome, or only extend it? If there is a specific thing the business could do with money that it cannot do without it, and that thing plausibly changes what the company is worth, raising has a clear case. If the capital would mostly fund more of what is already happening, the case is weaker. [...] A funding round prices a minority stake in new shares, puts capital into the company rather than into your hands, and leaves execution risk with you. A sale prices the whole company, settles in cash or buyer stock, and transfers that risk to the buyer. The headline numbers are therefore not comparable, and the decision turns on questions that have nothing to do with either: whether more capital would change what the business becomes, what your own cap table does to proceeds at realistic prices,

Title: Full article: The role of artificial intelligence in combating food fraud: a systematic literature review
4.   Critical Reviews in Food Science and Nutrition. 7.   The role of artificial intelligence in c .... # The role of artificial intelligence in combating food fraud: a systematic literature review. *   View PDF (open in a new window)PDF (open in a new window)View EPUB (open in a new window)EPUB (open in a new window). This study presents a systematic literature review evaluating the current state of artificial intelligence (AI) applications in combating food fraud. The aim was to examine the types of fraud detected by AI, the food products involved, the specific AI techniques used, and the performance evaluation metrics utilized. Most of the included studies focused on the detection of adulteration and mislabeling, particularly origin and quality mislabeling, with spices, herbs, meat and dairy being the most frequently investigated food product categories. Machine Learning (ML) and Deep Learning (DL) were the primary approaches utilized, ML was the most dominant, with Support Vector Machines (SVMs) and Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) emerging as the most frequently applied algorithms. Regarding the data types, spectral and imaging data were predominantly used, and most models were developed using supervised approaches. The findings underscore the importance of AI applied in food fraud detection and the need to explore underrepresented fraud types and food categories. Food Fraud is defined as “the deliberate and intentional substitution, addition, tampering, or misrepresentation of food, food ingredients, or food packaging; or false or misleading statements made about a product for economic gain”(Spink & Moyer Citation 2011). This systematic literature review evaluates the application of AI for the detection of food fraud. Aligned with the research questions, the study identifies investigated food commodities and fraud types, analyzes the input data modalities and algorithms employed and assesses performance metrics and data availability. The process includes the identification of research questions, the development of a search strategy through the selection of search terms and databases, the establishment of inclusion and exclusion criteria, the evaluation of the study quality, and finally, data extraction. *   RQ-1: Which food products and adulterants were investigated in the context of AI-based fraud detection?
